panels.rationale: Single Doppler ultrasound image of the right scrotum shows an avascular appendix testis with preserved testicular/epididymal flow and hydrocele, matching the caption and the diagnosis of torsion of the appendix testis in a neonate.

panels.figure_caption: Doppler ultrasonography revealed no blood flow to the appendix testis. Normal blood flow to the testis and epididymis were demonstrated. Right hydrocele was also identified.

Adjacent to the right testicle, an avascular extratesticular mass was noted, measuring approximately 6 mm (Figure 2). Based on the ultrasound and physical exam findings, the diagnosis of torsion of the appendix testis was considered. Clinically, the patient was stable and emergent causes of scrotal swelling were excluded. panels.rationale: Intraoperative photograph of undescended testicle at external inguinal ring showing testis (T), epididymis (e) and enlarged torsed appendix testis (AT) as captioned 'Torsion of the appendix Testis in an undescended testicle' and labelled 'Torsed appendix testis'. Shows specific gross manifestation of torsion_of_the_appendix_testis in cryptorchid location.
